"code": """"LightGBM with categorical feature encoding and missing-as-category handling."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
from lightgbm import LGBMClassifier


def fit_predict(train_csv: str, test_rows: list[dict[str, str]]) -> list[float]:
    train = pd.read_csv(train_csv)
    y = train.pop("y").astype(int)
    
    # Build test DataFrame preserving column order from train
    test = pd.DataFrame(test_rows, columns=train.columns)
    
    # Track which columns are categorical (non-numeric)
    categorical_cols = []
    for name in train.columns:
        try:
            pd.to_numeric(train[name])
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            categorical_cols.append(name)
    
    # Set all values to NaN where empty string appears, then ensure consistency
    for df in [train, test]:
        for col in train.columns:
            df[col] = df[col].replace('', pd.NA)
    
    # For categorical columns, ensure consistent dtypes (string/object)
    for col in categorical_cols:
        train[col] = train[col].astype('object')
        test[col] = test[col].astype('object')
    
    # Fit LightGBM - it handles missing values natively (treats them as a separate category)
    model = LGBMClassifier(
        random_state=20261114,
        n_jobs=1,
        verbosity=-1,
        categorical_feature=categorical_cols if categorical_cols else 'auto',
        missing=0  # LightGBM will handle missing as its own category
    )
    model.fit(train, y)
    return model.predict_proba(test)[:, 1].tolist()",
"notes": "Implemented LightGBM with explicit categorical_feature specification for non-numeric columns. Missing values are left as NA (pandas) which LightGBM natively handles as a separate category during split decisions. This avoids arbitrary imputation and leverages LightGBM's native categorical handling."
